title: fix(cli): the organization-ownership drop refusal says what 18.0 supports for a v17 database
body:
Fixes #24567
Clause-②: no — basis: refusal and help text only. No accept set, flag, exit code, JSON key or behaviour moves: the gate still holds back the whole `--allow-destructive` run with `refused_organization_ownership_unmigrated`, exit 1.

Row 3 of #24567 (rows 1–2 landed in #24592), `domain:cli` seat 1, claim `6273418995`. The drop-gate refusal that `os migrate apply --allow-destructive` gives on a 17.x-created database told the operator to run `os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN`, then `--apply --plan-file PLAN`, and 18.0 refuses that command on every database (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`). The refusal now says what 18.0 supports for a v17 database, in the boot refusal's terms, and names no step of that command. The command's `--help` examples and `os dev`'s way-on line had the same problem and are fixed with it.

## Before and after

Measured through the real CLI (`node packages/cli/bin/run.js`, built from each tree), on a 17.x-shaped SQLite made the way `apply-organization-ownership-gate.integration.test.ts` makes it: a v18 database created by `os migrate apply --yes --json` on an empty file, then `ALTER TABLE sys_platform_setting ADD COLUMN organization_id TEXT`. The command was `os migrate apply --allow-destructive --yes --database-url file:COPY.db`. It exited 1 both times, and the column was still there afterwards.

**Before** (base `65a8eeb7d`):

```text
✗ Refusing this --allow-destructive run: it would drop organization_id from sys_platform_setting, a drop the organization-ownership ceremony owns, and the ceremony has not verified on this database. No run of "os migrate organization-ownership --apply --plan-file FILE" is recorded on this database. Dropping the column first would turn every legacy organization row into an environment row without the ceremony's promotion or report. Run "os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN" to write and review its plan, then "os migrate organization-ownership --apply --plan-file PLAN"; it drops these columns itself, in its column-drops step, before it records the run verified. Nothing in this run was applied.
```

On the same file, the command it prescribed answers this (exit 1, no plan file written):

```text
✗ os migrate organization-ownership is not available in 18.0. 18.0 supports fresh installs only; the v17 → v18 upgrade path ships in an 18.x release. Keep a v17 database on a 17.x release until then. Nothing was read or written. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)
```

**After** (head `69778e478`):

```text
✗ Refusing this --allow-destructive run: it would drop organization_id from sys_platform_setting, a drop the organization-ownership ceremony owns, and the ceremony has not verified on this database. No run of the organization-ownership ceremony is recorded on this database. Dropping the column first would turn every legacy organization row into an environment row without the ceremony's promotion or report. 18.0 supports fresh installs only and does not upgrade a v17 database: keep a v17 database on a 17.x release until the 18.x release that carries the upgrade path, whose ceremony drops these columns itself, in its column-drops step, before it records the run verified. Nothing in this run was applied.
```

The boot refusal it now matches (`packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts`, v17-shape branch, not touched here): "18.0 does not upgrade a v17 database: keep this one on a 17.x release until the 18.x release that carries the upgrade path, and run these steps there." The drop gate cannot tell a v17 database from one 18.0 created (see the branch map), so it says "keep a v17 database" where the guard says "keep this one". That is also the wording of the command's own 18.0 refusal.

**`--json`**, the `detail` (the only prose the `--json` refusal carries):

- before: `No run of "os migrate organization-ownership --apply --plan-file FILE" is recorded on this database.`
- after: `No run of the organization-ownership ceremony is recorded on this database.`
- `message: refused_organization_ownership_unmigrated`, `tables: ["sys_platform_setting"]`, `marker: null`, `applied: []`, `created: []` and exit 1 are unchanged (measured).

**`os migrate organization-ownership --help`, EXAMPLES** — before: six invocations, every one refused in 18.0:

```text
$ os migrate organization-ownership
$ os migrate organization-ownership --out plans/v18-ownership.json
$ os migrate organization-ownership --database-url postgres://… --json
$ os migrate organization-ownership --apply --plan-file plans/v18-ownership.json --backup-taken
$ os migrate organization-ownership --fate-supplement host-fates.json
$ os migrate organization-ownership --dev
```

after (an override on the registered 18.0 class, `MigrateOrganizationOwnership`; the ceremony class `OrganizationOwnershipCeremony` keeps its six examples for the 18.x release that registers it):

```text
EXAMPLES
  Refused in 18.0, plan and apply alike: exit 1 with NOT_IMPLEMENTED, nothing
  read or written. Keep a v17 database on a 17.x release until the 18.x
  release that carries the upgrade path

    $ os migrate organization-ownership

  The same refusal as JSON: error, reason upgrade-unavailable, code
  NOT_IMPLEMENTED, and the detail

    $ os migrate organization-ownership --json
```

**`os dev`, the way-on line** (`utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts`; unit-measured, not run live). Before: "Run `os migrate organization-ownership --dev` (review its plan), then the same command with --apply --plan-file FILE --backup-taken, and start os dev again." After: "18.0 supports fresh installs only and does not upgrade a v17 database: keep a v17 development database on a 17.x release until the 18.x release that carries the upgrade path, and upgrade it there."

## Branch map of the refusal

The gate sits in `MigrateApply.run()` (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts`), below the drift report, above the confirmation prompt and above both writes.

| condition that selects it | what the operator sees | here |
|:--|:--|:--|
| no `drop_column organization_id` among the intended drift (`ceremonyOrganizationColumnDrops(intended)` is empty): every run without `--allow-destructive`, and every fresh 18.0 database whose objects keep their injected column | nothing from this gate | unchanged |
| a drop, and the `sys_migration` marker `adr-0131-organization-ownership` is verified | `organization_id on TABLES: the organization-ownership ceremony verified (DATE) — the drop may proceed.` | **kept**: true on any database, names no command |
| a drop, no marker (`flag` null) | detail `No run of the organization-ownership ceremony is recorded on this database.`, then the refusal above | **changed** |
| a drop, a marker that is not verified | detail `The last run of the organization-ownership ceremony recorded on this database (DATE) is not verified (N blocking item(s)).`, then the refusal above | **changed** (in 18.0 only a database a pre-18.0 ceremony ran on can carry one: 18.0 writes no marker) |
| `--json` on either refused branch | `{ message: refused_organization_ownership_unmigrated, tables, detail, marker }`, exit 1, with no prescription sentence, so only `detail` | **`detail` changed** |

**When does it fire on a fresh 18.0 install?** Only when an object newly declares no organization column over a table that already carries the injected one: `systemFields: { tenant: false }` on an existing object. I measured this at `69778e478`. On a database this 18.0 CLI created with one app object `acme_note` (its table gets `organization_id`), declaring `systemFields: { tenant: false }` makes the drift report offer `acme_note.organization_id … "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" to drop it.`, and that run is refused with the text above, exit 1, the column kept. The changeset for 6074eaf names this population on purpose: the ceremony plans that table.

**The premise that `organization-ownership --apply` IS supported on a fresh install does not hold at `origin/main`.** The registered `MigrateOrganizationOwnership.run()` refuses plan and apply on every database before it reads anything. Its doc says "plan and apply alike", and `organization-ownership.release-refusal.test.ts` pins this. So no branch of the old text was true in 18.0 on any database. Both refused branches change. The verified branch, the only one naming no command, is kept. The new text is true on a fresh database too: it says "keep a v17 database", not "keep this one". It gives such a database no way on, because 18.0 has none. That is an Acceptance note below, not a change here.

## Census

`git grep -n "organization-ownership"` over `packages/cli` (source, help text, README, CHANGELOG) and `content/docs`, at `65a8eeb7d`. These are the places that send a 17.x-created database's operator to the command:

| place | what it says | here |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts` drop-gate refusal (was `:586`–`:591`) | `Run "os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN" … then "… --apply --plan-file PLAN"` | **changed** (the defect) |
| `cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts` status lines, the `detail` (was `:575` / `:577`) | `No run of "os migrate organization-ownership --apply --plan-file FILE" is recorded …` / `The last run of "…" … is not verified` | **changed**: `--json` carries only this sentence, and it named the command with `--plan-file` |
| `cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts` verified line (`:607`) | `the organization-ownership ceremony verified (DATE) — the drop may proceed.` | **kept**: true, names no command |
| `cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts` examples (`:330`–`:337`) | six plan and apply invocations | **kept on the ceremony class** (shown nowhere in 18.0, and true for the 18.x release that registers it); **overridden on the registered 18.0 class** (`:1134`) |
| `cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts` description and flag help | 18.0's description already opens "Refused in 18.0, which supports fresh installs only: …"; the flag lines describe the ceremony's flags | **kept**: the help's first sentence says refused, and examples now show the refusal |
| `cli/src/utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts` `manual` (`:127`) | "Run `os migrate organization-ownership --dev` (review its plan), then the same command with --apply …" | **changed**: in 18.0 it printed right under the ceremony's own NOT_IMPLEMENTED line, and on a non-local database it was the whole answer |
| `cli/src/utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts` `again` (`:178`, used `:194`, `:207`) | "run `os migrate organization-ownership --dev --apply --plan-file …`" | **kept**: reached only after a plan succeeded, which 18.0 never does |
| `cli/src/commands/dev.ts:822` | "This development database is still in the v17 organization-ownership shape — upgrading it in place (a copy is kept first)…" | **kept**: names no command (see Acceptance notes) |
| `cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-{apply,plan,inventory,column-drops}.ts`, `reportReservationText` in `organization-ownership.ts` | the ceremony's own messages | **kept**: printed only when the ceremony class runs, which in 18.0 is only its tests |
| `cli/src/commands/serve.ts`, `schema-migrate.ts`, `migrate-occupancy-gate.ts`, `security-catalog-overlays.ts`, `schema-migration-plugins.ts`, `vitest.config.ts` | comments only; `serve` prints the runtime boot guard's text | **kept**: the boot guard is held off and is the reference |
| `cli/README.md` | no hit | — |
| `cli/CHANGELOG.md` (6074eaf, dd29bbe, 4369677 and others) | released entries prescribing the ceremony | **kept**: release-owned, they record what those releases did, never edited in a code PR |
| `cli/src/**/*.test.ts` (about 35 files) | the ceremony's tests run the class directly | **kept**; three pin files updated, one added (Tests) |
| `content/docs` pages generated from the CLI | none: `content/docs/references/` is generated from the spec and has no hit, and `deployment/cli.mdx` is hand-written (`scripts/docs-audit/handwritten-docs.json`) | — |
| hand-written `content/docs` | see Acceptance notes | not edited here: `domain:devx`'s |

## Tests

At head `69778e478`, after `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/cli^...' build` (lock VERDICT command-exit 0) and the CLI's own build:

- New `src/commands/migrate/apply.organization-ownership-refusal.test.ts` (unit tier: no boot, no driver). It runs the real command with the boot, the occupancy probe, the exit and the marker read replaced. For both refused marker states (none, unverified) it pins: the human face exits 1, the refusal names the table, it does not match `os migrate organization-ownership|--plan-file|organization-ownership --out`, it names the 17.x and the 18.x release, and nothing is written. It pins the same absence on the `--json` `detail`. A verified-marker control reaches the writes and exits 0.
- `apply-organization-ownership-gate.integration.test.ts`: the `detail` pin `/os migrate organization-ownership --apply/` is now `/organization-ownership ceremony/` plus the same absence, on the real command against a v17-shape SQLite table. Run locally because the diff edits it: 5/5 passed.
- `organization-ownership.release-refusal.test.ts`: new case. Every example of the registered class names the command without `--out` / `--apply` / `--plan-file` / `--fate-supplement`, and its description names `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. The ceremony class keeps an `--apply --plan-file` example.
- `dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.test.ts`: the non-local case's pin `toContain('os migrate organization-ownership --dev')` is now the 17.x release plus the absence of the command and of `--plan-file`. The refused-plan case gains the same.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --project unit`: **314 files, 4640 tests passed** (run at `c6cea949b`; the last commit changes only the wording these pins read, and they were re-run at `69778e478`: 4 files 99 tests, plus the integration file 5/5).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit` program lists all seven edited `.ts` files, 0 errors; `check:test-typecheck` OK, ledger unchanged).
- **Ablation** of the pin at `69778e478`, via `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the old prescription was put back into the refusal (anchor `'until the 18.x release that carries the upgrade path, whose ceremony drops these columns itself, in its '`, x1 → x0; blob `7a6414669b72` → `e8260625ac6f`). Result: **2 failed | 3 passed**. The two human-face cases went red; the two `--json` cases and the control stayed green, because the mutation touched the message, not the `detail`. Restored blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty. The subject resolves through a relative `./apply.js` import (src, no `dist`), so no build leg was owed. A first attempt at `c6cea949b` was refused by the tool as a no-op: its replacement contained its anchor, so the anchor count did not move and nothing was measured. It was re-run with a new anchor (same 2 red).

## Gates

All at head `69778e478`, with every exit code captured before any pipe:

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` derived **68 commands**: a change set of 8 paths, 288 changed lines against merge base `65a8eeb7d`. **All 68 exit 0.** `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` first exited 3 with PREREQUISITE NOT MET, because some packages this diff does not touch had no `dist`. Those attempts measured nothing. After `turbo run build` of those packages (75 tasks, all cache hits), both re-ran: `✓ check:dual-build-cjs-loads — 111 published require entry point(s) across 69 package(s) load` and `check-i18n-coverage: OK (14 config(s), 621 baselined untranslated string(s), none new)`.
- The **11 declared-wide families** (`check:init-service-contract`, `live-db-isolation`, `meta-type-normalized`, `optional-error-sink`, `resume-authority-declared`, `route-envelope`, `runner-env-posture`, `settings-bind-window`, `startup-registry-verdict`, `verify-stand-in`, `wildcard-fallthrough`): all exit 0.
- The `--ran` reconciliation answers `Run reconciliation — 68 derived, 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.` That zero is derived from the recorded exit codes. The 11 wide families are recorded as outside the derivation.
- **`pnpm lint`** (`eslint . --no-inline-config`, the full union): exit 0.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 7 changed `.ts` files: exit 0, nothing printed. The control-byte self-scan of the changed files found none.
- Lines from the gates: `✓ check-adr-0087-registration: this PR adds no declared-breaking changeset (1 non-breaking changeset(s) seen).` · `✓ This diff introduces no major bump.` · `✓ doc authoring guard: 19124 customer-facing string(s) across 1437 spec sources clean`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Row 1's open maintainer question is touched, not answered.** Like the boot refusal, this text tells the operator to keep a v17 database on a 17.x release. A v18 `os serve` boot may already have added v18 schema to that database. That question stays with the maintainer. `os migrate apply` itself writes nothing before this refusal: the gate is above every write, and the boot defers DDL.
- **A database 18.0 created can reach this gate with no way on in 18.0** (measured above, `acme_note`). An object that newly declares `systemFields: { tenant: false }` over its injected `organization_id` makes the drift report prescribe `--allow-destructive`, and this gate refuses it. By source, the v18 boot guard then refuses `os serve` with "This database is still in the v17 organization-ownership shape … keep this one on a 17.x release" (`findV17ShapeTables` reads only `tenant === false` plus the physical column). Its `os serve` half was not measured. The 18.0 ruling covers v17 upgrades; this population is outside it. Reported to the seat for a decision. The text here makes no claim about it that is false.
- **Hand-written `content/docs` (`domain:devx`), not edited:** `deployment/cli.mdx:1027`–`:1029` describes the drop gate as waiting for "a verified `os migrate organization-ownership --apply --plan-file FILE` run", with no 18.0 qualifier there. `deployment/cli.mdx:1477`–`:1494` has an 18.0 callout over a fenced plan and apply block. `deployment/cli.mdx:200`–`:222` (os dev) has a callout, then "run the ceremony yourself" and "they refuse and name the command". `concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx:109` says "an 18.x `os serve` refuses to start … until the v18 migration ceremony (`os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN`, then `--apply --plan-file PLAN`)". `permissions/capabilities.mdx:220` and `permissions/permission-sets.mdx:399` describe what `--apply` does. The hits in `deployment/environment-variables.mdx`, `deployment/install-modes.mdx`, `ui/public-data-collection.mdx` and `releases/v18/index.mdx` are the ADR-0131 file name in a URL.
- **The same family outside `packages/cli`, held off here:** `metadata-core/src/legacy-organization-row.ts:78` ("Run `os migrate organization-ownership` on this database first."), `metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts:1739` ("`os migrate organization-ownership`, then the same command with --apply"), `plugins/plugin-security/src/catalog-reference-report.ts:437`–`:438` (plan, then `--apply --backup-taken --plan-file`). Also two of the runtime boot guard's three refusals: the unverified-marker branch and the read-failure branch name the steps with no 18.0 sentence. And the spec's ADR-0087 entries `18.sys-metadata{,-audit,-commit,-history}-organization-column-retired`, `18.ups-permission-set-id-column-retired`, `18.sharing-rule-declared-mirror-retired` and `18.cli-organization-ownership-apply-plan-file-required` (`domain:spec`). Listed in the report for the seat to fold into one family card.
- `dev.ts:822` still prints "upgrading it in place" before an 18.0 upgrade that always stops at the plan's refusal. The lines after it now say why and what to do. It names no command, so it is kept.
